en: The Mañjuśrī-mūla-ekākṣara-dhāraṇī Sūtra from the Mahāvaipulya Bodhisattvapiṭaka,
translated during the Great Tang Dynasty by [the master from] Kaśmīra in North India.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Ratnabhadra: Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was dwelling in the Jewel-Adorned Bodhimanda of the Śuddhāvāsa Heaven, together with a great assembly of bodhisattvas and the host of the Śuddhāvāsa devas.
At that time, the World-Honored One, out of great kindness and great compassion,
addressed all the hosts of devas in this assembly,
saying: "Listen well, all of you, to the ritual of the wheel-mantra practiced by the youth Mañjuśrī."
For the sake of protecting all sentient beings,
I shall now reveal and proclaim for you all the Great King of Secret Heart-Mantras belonging to all Tathāgatas.
If there be anyone who recites it,
I declare that this person shall have already upheld all mantras, which are entirely perfected;
all that they undertake shall attain accomplishment.
There is nothing superior to this.
You all should know that among all dhāraṇīs,
this is the King of Great Divine Dhāraṇīs, possessing great supernatural power.
If any son or daughter of good family is able to receive and uphold this,
the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta will constantly come to protect them,
whether during their waking hours or within their dreams.
It manifests physical forms and various auspicious signs,
enabling this person to give rise to great joy.
Sons of good family, this King of Mantras is even capable of gathering the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta under its power.
How much more so for other bodhisattvas, as well as the multitudes of mundane and supramundane worthies and sages.
Furthermore, good son,
this mantra can eliminate all calamities, obstacles, and all evil dreams.
It can eliminate all enemies, all five heinous crimes, the four grave offenses, and the ten evil karmas;
it can also counteract all wicked, heterodox, and inauspicious incantations,
and further accomplish all virtuous deeds through great diligence.
One should know that this mantra is the most supreme among all worldly and world-transcending mantras;
it is the heart-essence of all Buddhas, capable of fulfilling every single aspiration.
If one uses threads of five colors to tie a mantra-cord around their neck,
it will protect their body and cause all their aspirations to be fulfilled.
All shall attain perfection without exception.
He then spoke the mantra, saying:
*Oṃ cili cili*. O sons of the Buddhas, this mantra can extinguish all evil, heterodox, and malevolent spirits.
All these spirits are the auspicious dharmas of all Buddhas;
they are also able to accomplish all divine mantras.
Those who recite this mantra—
It can cause sentient beings to give rise to great loving-kindness;
it can cause sentient beings to give rise to great compassion;
and all obstacles shall be completely extinguished.
All aspirations shall be fully satisfied;
even before the rite is performed,
one will be able to accomplish matters according to one's wishes.
If one generates the unsurpassed mind of great bodhicitta and recites it once, its power can protect oneself;
if one recites it twice, its power can protect one's companions.
If recited three times, its power can protect all those within a single house.
If recited four times, its power can protect all those within a single city.
If recited five times, its power can protect all those within a single kingdom.
If one recites it six times, its power can protect the people of one world-system.
If one recites it seven times, its power can protect the people of the four world-systems.
If one recites it once at dawn, [the same applies].
If one rinses the face with consecrated water, it will cause those who see one to rejoice;
if one perfumes one's clothes with consecrated incense, it likewise causes those who see one to rejoice.
If one suffers from toothache:
Chanting the mantra while chewing a tooth-stick for cleaning the teeth will immediately cure whatever pain one suffers from doing so. Furthermore,
if there is a woman experiencing difficulties during childbirth, [the same shall apply].
Take the root of the aṭarūṣaka or the root of the laṅgalīka;
enchant it seven times with mantras and grind it with water free of insects.
If it is applied to the umbilicus of a woman in labor, the child will be born easily.
Or, if a man is struck by an arrow such that the barb has entered deep into the sinews and bones and cannot be extracted, [applying this remedy] will cause it to come out.
Take three *liang* of clarified butter (*ghṛta*) and recite the mantra over it one hundred and eight times.
Place it upon the wound and consume it;
the arrowhead will then be extracted.
If a woman has not given birth to a son or daughter for five years, or even for twenty or thirty years,
whether she herself is ill or her husband is ill.
For various illnesses such as those caused by possession by malevolent spirits,
or for those struck by poison,
one should take five *liang* of clarified butter that is ten years old or more.
Place one *liang* of peacock feathers within clarified butter and recite the mantra over them twenty-one times.
Boil them and pound them into a powder.
Add one *liang* of rock honey and three *harītakī* fruits.
Remove the kernels and take the husks;
blend them together and recite the mantra over them one hundred and eight times.
Always consume the entire amount at dawn on an empty stomach.
Within seven days, a son or daughter will be born.
If one suffers from a headache, recite the mantra over a crow’s wing feather seven times and brush it against the head of the afflicted person;
the pain will immediately be relieved and cured.
If one suffers from malaria that recurs every day, every two days, or even up to every seven days,
or if it is a chronic condition,
one should cook gruel with pure milk.
Take one *liang* of high-quality ghee, recite the mantra over it one hundred and eight times, and give it to the patient to consume; they will immediately be cured.
To speak briefly, O sons of good family:
If one wishes to compound all medicinal decoctions or intends to take them, one must first recite this with a sincere mind twenty-one times; then one will quickly attain one's wish.
Furthermore, O son of good family, if there are any sentient beings...
He will be seized by a flying-head ghost (pīṭhaja),
who will rub his own face with his hands and recite a mantra one hundred and eight times while assuming a terrifying appearance.
Then, with the left hand, form the Jātaka mudrā:
bend the thumb into the palm and press it down with the four fingers behind it.
Immediately clenching his fist,
he stared with bulging eyes and recited this mantra silently;
consequently, the ailment of the one being treated was instantly eliminated.
If a person suffers from any illness caused by ghosts,
one should recite the mantra over their right hand one hundred and eight times and burn frankincense (an-shi-xiang) to fumigate it.
Form the *jātaka-mudrā* with the left hand;
rub the patient’s head with the right hand, and their ailment will immediately be cured.
Should there be enemies or various evil dreams, [the same shall apply].
When various fears cause the body and mind to be unsettled,
one should tie a mantra-cord of seven-colored threads into the shape of a lotus,
or the shape of a wheel, or the shape of a vajra.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times,
burn frankincense to fumigate it,
and wear it around the neck for seven days.
All calamities and misfortunes shall be entirely dispelled.
Alternatively, grind ox-gallstone (gośīrṣa) to make ink,
and upon clean paper or a fine silk cloth, [inscribe the mantra].
Draw the form of the one to be terrified;
around its four sides, encircle it with the syllable *ṭaṃ*,
or draw a lotus, or the syllable *cakram*.
Alternatively, one may surround it with the svastika, the śaṅkha, the makara, the vajrāṅkuśa, or the precious vase;
by reciting the mantra seven times, whatever fears there may be will be immediately dispelled.
O sons of good family, if you wish to pass through places of peril—such as those infested by lions, tigers, wolves, venomous snakes, enemies, or bandits—[you should do so].
One must purify both body and mind;
one must not associate with women, nor consume any of the five pungent roots, alcohol, meat, rape-seed, or coriander.
One should give rise to thoughts of great compassion toward all sentient beings.
If one recites this mantra with a sincere mind forty-nine times over it,
all enemies and evildoers will naturally retreat and disperse;
even if they encounter the practitioner, there shall be none who do not rejoice.
Good sons, even if all sentient beings were to spend a single kalpa or immeasurable kalpas,
they would not even be able to hear the name of this mantra.
How much more so for those who actually behold it and recite it with single-minded devotion! Even if one were to fill Jambudvīpa with the seven precious jewels, elephants, and horses,
these would still be things subject to destruction within this world.
This dhāraṇī mantra enables sentient beings to constantly obtain peace and security in both the present life and future lives,
and to always be accompanied by the Tathāgatas and the assembly of great bodhisattvas as their kin.
Whether for one's own sake or for the sake of others,
all that is wished for shall be attained;
therefore, one should earnestly conceive the thought that this is difficult to encounter.
Do not treat this with contempt or give rise to a doubting mind.
This is the *Mañjuśrī-mūla-ekākṣara-dhāraṇī-sūtra* from within the *Mahāvaipulya-bodhisattvapiṭaka-sūtra*.
